summary: Jamie Hubbard works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University under Kazuo Okabe and earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. In 2016, he was attested as an endowed professor at Smith College.

Jampa Losang Panglung (1939–2022) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Geshe Lharamapa at Sera Monastery and his Magister and doctorate at the University of Munich. From around 1978 to 2004, he worked at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences.
Jampa Mackenzie Stewart is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche and the 3rd Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.
Jampa Samten is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Director (attested 1991) and later Professor (attested 2015) at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Jamsrangiin Tseveen (1881–1942) worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University, headed the Mongolian Academy of Sciences (~1921–1930), and worked at the Russian Academy of Sciences' Institute of Oriental Studies (1932–1937).

Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö (1893–1959) was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar and master in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He succeeded Jamyang Chökyi Wangpo and studied under numerous traditional masters, including Khenpo Thupten, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo (1820–1892) was a prominent figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Minling Trichen Gyurme Sangye Kunga, Shechen Gyurme Thutob Namgyal, and Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye.
Jamyang Sherab Chokyi Nangwa studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Jan Chozen Bays (b. 1945) is a Buddhist studies and religious studies practitioner. She studied at Swarthmore College, UC San Diego, and under Taizan Maezumi and Shodo Harada. She served as a teacher in Oregon and abbess of Great Vow Zen Monastery.
Jan Dolensky is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2013).

Jan Fontein (1927–2017) specialized in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history/archaeology. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Theodoor Paul Galestin, served as a curator at the Rijksmuseum, and was curator of Asiatic art at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1966–1992).

Jan Gonda (1905–1991) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Utrecht University under Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff and at Leiden University. He held the Chair of Sanskrit (1929) and was Professor of Indology (1932–1976) at Utrecht University.

Jan Jakob Maria de Groot (1854–1921) was a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He studied at Leiden University and under Georg von der Gabelentz, later serving as professor at Leiden University (1891–1912) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1912–1921).

Jan Jaworski (1903–1945) was a scholar of sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Warsaw from circa 1923 to 1928, and also studied under Stanisław Schayer and Jean Przyluski.

Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak (1889–1954) was a sinologist who studied at Leiden, the Sorbonne, and Humboldt University under Jan Jakob Maria de Groot and others. He served as professor of Chinese language and literature at Leiden University from 1930 to 1954.

Jan N. Bremmer (b. 1944) works in religious studies and history/archaeology. He earned degrees from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and the University of Amsterdam, taught at Utrecht University (1974–1990), and held the Chair of Religious Studies at the University of Groningen (1990–2009).

Jan Nattier (b. 1949) specializes in Buddhist studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She studied at Indiana University and Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi. She held professorships at Indiana University (1992–2005) and Soka University (2004–2010), among other appointments.

Jan Peter F. Hintelmann specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Marianne Pieper and also studied under traditional teachers including Thupten Nyandak, Tenzin Kunga, Sonam Senge, and Geshe Sonam Rinchen.

Jan Pieter Hogendijk (b. 1955) works in the history of mathematics. He earned his doctorate at Utrecht University under G. J. Toomer and held professorships in the history of mathematics at Leiden University (2004–2009) and Utrecht University (appointed 2005).

Jan Westerhoff (b. 1976) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Cambridge under Michael Potter and from SOAS. Around 2013, he became Professor of Buddhist Philosophy at the University of Oxford and Fellow at Lady Margaret Hall.
